cells.tense: You are starting something here, and you are holding it with an open hand.
cells.ask: Offer one thing you've been keeping to yourself to the person most likely to carry it further than you.
cells.core:
You're at the beginning of something worth keeping — a practice, a way of doing things, a piece of knowledge that has your fingerprints on it. You know how to hold it without squeezing. You're not forcing your version on anyone, and you're not hiding it either. You put it out and let people try it.

That balance is rarer than it sounds. The thing stays alive because people can move it around and make it theirs. Keeping it there costs something: being willing to be surprised by what it turns into. The thing you're starting doesn't need to stay yours. It just needs to get into the right hands.
cells.sheetLine: You hold it open, and that's what lets it travel.
cells.verb: beginning something that others can pick up and carry
cells.place: among the practices and meanings that get handed down

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future where this thing has to already be solid, and you are gripping it too hard.
cells.ask: Leave one piece of what you're making unfinished on purpose, and say so to whoever looks at it next.
cells.core:
You're out ahead of this — already defending a version that isn't even built yet. A conversation about the practice or the way you do things turns into a preemptive explanation. It should be right before anyone sees it, so nobody gets a say in making it.

But the beginning stage doesn't survive that much protection. Nothing gets handed down if it doesn't get handed over — and here the beginning is exactly the thing that should be passed along wet. The thing you're building wants to be tangible enough to share, not sealed enough to be untouchable. Start with one part you can show while it's still wet. Let someone hold the half-formed version and find out it doesn't break.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding a door before anything's built.

cells.tense: You are standing behind a moment that already passed, still deciding whether to begin.
cells.ask: Name one thing you know how to do and show it to someone today, even briefly — no long explanation.
cells.core:
There is something you have known or carried for a while now, and you are not putting it into the world. The beginning was there. You walked past it. Maybe it was too obvious or too small or you were not sure anyone wanted it. So it stays in your head where it cannot be argued with or improved.

Meanwhile the practice you care about is missing what you would bring to it. That is not a failure of yours. It is a gap where your offering used to be. The thing does not need a perfect launch. It needs one showing — one time you let someone see a thing you know how to do, brown edges showing. That is enough to close the distance.
cells.sheetLine: You have something, and it's been waiting at the door.

cells.tense: You are already shaping what gets passed on, and you are calling it the natural way things are.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you do the same way whenever it comes up, and say out loud: this is how I keep it.
cells.core:
You are already doing it. The way you say a thing, the order you do things in, the stories you reach for when someone asks — that is transmission. It runs so smoothly it gets described as just how things are done. No one deliberately chose that. It just happened.

But a choice is being made each time you repeat that phrase or keep that practice going. You are spending something on it — attention, time, the effort it takes. That effort has your mark on it, and credit has been going to the water instead of the person carrying the bucket. Claim one piece of it. Not to feel proud, just to be accurate about what is actually happening.
cells.sheetLine: You are keeping it alive, and that work has your mark.
